verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah son of Helkiah. And it happened in the month of Secheelu, in the twentieth year, that I was in Susa Abira.
verses.1:2: And Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and men of Judah, and I asked them about those who had been saved, who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
verses.1:3: And they said to me, "Those who remain, who were left from the captivity there in the province, in the city, are in great distress and in reproach; and the walls of Jerusalem are torn down, and its gates were burned with fire."
verses.1:4: And it happened, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
verses.1:5: And I said, "Please, not so, Lord God of heaven, the Mighty One, the great and awesome, keeping the covenant and Your mercy for those who love Him and for those who keep His commandments:
verses.1:6: let Your ear now be attentive and Your eyes be open to hear the prayer of Your servant, which I am praying before You today, day and night, concerning the sons of Israel Your servants, and confessing regarding the sins of the sons of Israel which we have sinned against You; both I and the house of my father have sinned.
verses.1:7: We have utterly dissolved, and we have not kept the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments which You commanded Moses Your servant.
verses.1:8: Remember now the word which You commanded Moses Your servant, saying, 'If you break faith, I will scatter you among the peoples;
verses.1:9: and if you return to Me, and keep My commandments and do them, if your dispersion is from the end of heaven, from there I will gather them, and I will bring them into the place which I have chosen to make My name dwell there.'
verses.1:10: And they are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and by Your mighty hand.
verses.1:11: Please, not so, but let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who desire to fear Your name; and grant success now to Your servant today, and grant him compassion before this man." And I was a eunuch to the king.
verses.2:1: And it happened in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that wine was before me; and I took the wine and gave it to the king, and there was no one else before him.
verses.2:2: And the king said to me, "Why is your face sad, and you are not unwell? This is nothing other than sadness of heart." And I was very greatly afraid.
verses.2:3: And I said to the king, "May the king live forever. Why should my face not be sad, because the city, the house of the tombs of my fathers, has been laid waste, and its gates were devoured by fire?"
verses.2:4: And the king said to me, "What is this that you are asking about?" And I prayed to the God of heaven.
verses.2:5: And I said to the king, "If it is good to the king, and if your servant is pleasing before you, that you send him to Judah, to the city of the tombs of my fathers, then I will rebuild it."
verses.2:6: And the king, and the concubine who was sitting beside him, said to me, "How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" And it was pleasing before the king, and he sent me, and I gave him a set time.
verses.2:7: And I said to the king, "If it is good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the River, so that they may let me pass through until I come to Judah,
verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the park that belongs to the king, so that he may give me timber to roof the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will enter." And the king gave them to me, according to the good hand of God.
verses.2:9: And I came to the governors beyond the River, and gave them the letters of the king; and the king sent with me commanders of an army and horsemen.
verses.2:10: And Sanballat the Horonite heard, and it was displeasing to them that a man had come to seek good for the sons of Israel.
verses.2:11: And I came to Jerusalem, and I was there three days.
verses.2:12: And I arose by night, I and a few men with me, and I did not tell anyone what God was putting into my heart to do with Israel, and there was no animal with me except the animal on which I was riding.
verses.2:13: And I went out by the Gate of Golela, and toward the mouth of the Spring of the Figs, and to the Dung Gate; and I was crushing at the wall of Jerusalem, which they are tearing down, and its gates were devoured by fire.
verses.2:14: And I passed on to the Gate of Aina and to the Pool of the King, and there was no place for the animal under me to pass through.
verses.2:15: And I was going up along the wall, up the torrents, by night, and I was crushing at the wall; and I was at the Valley Gate, and I returned.
verses.2:16: And the guards did not know why I had gone and what I was doing; and until then I had not told the Jews, or the priests, or the nobles, or the rest who were doing the works.
verses.2:17: And I said to them, "You see the distress in which we are, how Jerusalem is desolate and its gates were given to fire. Come, and let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be a reproach."
verses.2:18: And I told them of the hand of God, which is good upon me, and also about the words of the king that he spoke to me; and I said, "Let us rise and build." And their hands were strengthened for good.
verses.2:19: And Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard, and they mocked us, and came upon us and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Or are you rebelling against the king?"
verses.2:20: And I returned word to them and said to them, "The God of heaven, He will grant us success, and we are His pure servants, and let us build; but for you there is no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
verses.3:1: And Eliashib the high priest and his brothers the priests rose up and built the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and set up its doors, and as far as the Tower of the Hundred they consecrated it, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
verses.3:2: And at the hands of the men, the sons of Jericho, and at the hands of the sons of Zabaur son of Imri.
verses.3:3: And the sons of Hasan built the Fish Gate; they roofed it, and roofed its doors and its bolts and its bars.
verses.3:4: And at their side it held to Ramoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz. And at their side Zadok son of Baanah held fast.
verses.3:5: And at their side the Tekoites held fast, and Adoreem did not bring their neck into their service.
verses.3:6: And Joeiaa son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Badiah repaired the Gate of Jeshanah; they roofed it, and set up its doors and its bolts and its bars.
verses.3:8: And at their side Hananiah son of Joiakim repaired, and they left Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
verses.3:9: And at their side Rephaiah, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
verses.3:10: And at their side Jedaiah son of Heromath repaired, even opposite his house. And at his side Hatuth son of Hasbanam repaired.
verses.3:11: And second, Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired, and as far as the Tower of the Nathurim.
verses.3:12: And at his side Shallum son of Heliah, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.
verses.3:13: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they built it, and set up its doors and its bolts and its bars, and a thousand cubits on the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
verses.3:14: And Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-acham, repaired the Dung Gate, he and his sons; and they covered it, and set up its doors and its bolts and its bars,
verses.3:15: and the wall of the Pool of the Fleeces for the king's shearing, and as far as the stairs going down from the city of David.
verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of the district of Besor, repaired as far as the garden of the tomb of David, and as far as the pool that had been made, and as far as Beth-abarim.
verses.3:17: After him the Levites repaired: Basuth son of Bani. At his side Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
verses.3:18: After him their brothers repaired: Bedei son of Henadalat, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
verses.3:19: And at his side Azzur son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired a second section of the tower of the ascent joining the corner.
verses.3:20: After him Baruch son of Zabu repaired a second section from the corner as far as the door of Beth-eliashib the high priest.
verses.3:21: After him Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakob repaired a second section from the door of Beth-eliashib as far as the end of Beth-eliashib.
verses.3:22: And after him the priests, the men of Hachechar, repaired.
verses.3:23: And after him Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After him Azariah son of Madasel, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his house.
verses.3:24: After him Bani son of Henadad repaired a second section from Beth-azariah as far as the corner and as far as the bend.
verses.3:25: Palal son of Evei opposite the corner, and the projecting tower from the house of the king, the upper one, which belongs to the court of the guard. And after him, Pedaiah son of Parosh.
verses.3:26: And the Katheinim were living in Ophel as far as the garden of the Water Gate toward the east, and the projecting tower.
verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites repaired a second section opposite the great projecting tower and as far as the wall of Ophel.
verses.3:28: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each man opposite his house.
verses.3:29: After him, Zadok son of Immer opposite his house. And after him Shemaiah son of Echeniah, the keeper of the house of the east, repaired.
verses.3:30: After him Hananiah son of Telemiah and Hanum, the sixth son of Sele, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his treasury.
verses.3:31: After him Malchijah son of Saraphi repaired as far as Beth-anathim, and the peddlers opposite the Gate of Miphkad and as far as the middle of the bend.
verses.3:32: And in the middle of the ascent of the Sheep Gate, the smiths and the peddlers repaired.
verses.3:33: And it happened, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that it seemed displeasing to him, and he became very angry, and he was mocking the Jews.
verses.3:34: And he said before his brothers, "Is this the army of Samaria, that these Jews are building their own city?"
verses.3:35: And Tobiah the Ammonite came beside him; and they said to one another, "Surely they will not sacrifice or eat in their place? Will not a fox climb up and tear down their wall of stones?"
verses.3:36: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of scorn, and turn back their reproach upon their head, and give them over to scorn in a land of captivity,
verses.3:37: and do not cover over lawlessness.
verses.4:1: And it happened, when Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabs and the Ammonites heard that the growth went up on the walls of Jerusalem, that the breaches began to be closed up, it appeared very evil to them.
verses.4:2: And they all gathered together to come to do battle in Jerusalem.
verses.4:3: And we prayed to our God, and we stationed watchmen against them day and night because of them.
verses.4:4: And Judah said, "The strength of the enemies has been crushed, and there is a large crowd, and we will not be able to build on the wall."
verses.4:5: And those oppressing us said, "They will not know and will not see until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work."
verses.4:6: And it happened, when the Jews who lived next to them came, they said to us, "They are coming up from all the places against us."
verses.4:7: And I stationed them in the lowest parts of the place behind the wall in the sheltered places, and I stationed the people by clans with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
verses.4:8: And I looked, and I rose up and said to the nobles and to the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them; remember our God, who is great and awesome, and do battle for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses."
verses.4:9: And it happened, when our enemies heard that it was known to us, God frustrated their counsel; and all of us returned to the wall, each man to his work.
verses.4:10: And it happened from that day that half of the shaken-out ones were doing the work, and half of them were holding fast, and there were spears and shields and the bows and the breastplates, and the rulers were behind the whole house of Judah,
verses.4:11: who were building on the wall. And those lifting with the carrying-straps were in arms; with one hand each was doing the work itself, and with one was holding the javelin.
verses.4:12: And as for the builders, each man had his sword strapped at his waist, and they were building; and the one sounding the horn was next to him.
verses.4:13: And I said to the nobles and to the rulers and to the rest of the people, "The work is broad and great, and we are scattered on the wall, each man far from his brother.
verses.4:14: In whatever place you hear the sound of the horn, there you will gather to us, and our God will fight for us."
verses.4:15: And we were doing the work, and half of them were holding the spears from the rising until the dawn, until the coming out of the stars.
verses.4:16: And at that time I said to the people, "Spend the night in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be a watch for you, and the day work."
verses.4:17: And I was there, and the men of the watch behind me, and not a man among us was taking off his clothes.
verses.5:1: And there was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.
verses.5:2: And there were some saying, "With our sons and with our daughters we are many; and we will get grain, and we will eat and live."
verses.5:3: And there are some saying, "Our fields and our vineyards and our houses, we are pledging them; and we will get grain and eat."
verses.5:4: And there are some saying, "We have borrowed silver for the taxes of the king—our fields and our vineyards and our houses.
verses.5:5: Now like the flesh of our brothers is our flesh, like our sons are their sons; and look, we are subjugating our sons and our daughters to be female slaves, and some of our daughters are being subjugated; and there is no power in our hand, and our fields and our vineyards belong to the nobles."
verses.5:6: And I was very grieved when I heard their outcry and these words.
verses.5:7: And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended against the nobles and the rulers and said to them, "You are demanding an exaction, each man from his brother." And I held a great assembly against them,
verses.5:8: and I said to them, "We have bought our brothers the Jews who were being sold to the nations of our own free will; and are you selling our brothers?" And they kept silent and did not find a word.
verses.5:9: And I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good; not in this way, in the fear of our God, will you depart from the reproach of our enemies.
verses.5:10: And my brothers and my acquaintances and I placed silver and grain with them, yet we gave up this exaction.
verses.5:11: Now you yourselves return this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive trees, and their houses, and from the silver, the grain and the wine, and bring them out for yourselves."
verses.5:12: And they said, "We will give it back and will require nothing from them; thus we will do just as you say." And I called the priests and made them swear to do according to this word.
verses.5:13: And I shook out my cloak and said, "Thus may God shake out every man who will not uphold this word from his house and from his labor, and thus he will be shaken out and empty." And all the assembly said, "Amen," and they praised the Lord; and the people performed this word.
verses.5:14: From the day that he commanded me to be their ruler in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even until the thirty-second year of Arsenatha, twelve years, I and our brothers did not eat their extortion.
verses.5:15: And the former extortions that were before me, they laid heavily upon them, and they took from them in bread and in wine, lastly silver, forty didrachmas, and their shaken-out ones exercise authority over the people; and I did not do so because of the fear of God.
verses.5:16: And in the work of the wall of these people I did not take hold; I did not buy a field; and all those who were gathered there were at the work.
verses.5:17: And the Jews, one hundred and fifty men, and those coming to us from the nations around us, were at my table.
verses.5:18: And there was prepared for one day one calf, and choice sheep and a goat were prepared for me, and every ten days, among all things, wine in abundance; and along with these things I did not demand the bread of extortion, because the servitude was heavy upon this people.
verses.5:19: Remember me, God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.
verses.6:1: And it happened, when it was heard by Sanballat and Tobiah and Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies that the wall had been built and no breath was left in them—until that time I had not set up doors in the gates—
verses.6:2: that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, and let us gather together in the villages in the plain of Ono." And they were planning to do evil to me.
verses.6:3: And I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work, and I will not be able to come down, so that the work may not stop; as soon as I finish it, I will come down to you."
verses.6:4: And they sent to me according to this word, and I sent to them according to these things.
verses.6:5: And Sanballat sent to me his servant, and an open letter in his hand.
verses.6:6: And it was written in it, "Among the nations it has been heard that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; for this reason you are building the wall, and you will be king for them.
verses.6:7: And in addition to these things, you have appointed prophets for yourself, so that you may sit in Jerusalem as king over Judah; and now these words will be reported to the king. And now come, let us take counsel together."
verses.6:8: And I sent to him, saying, "It has not happened according to these words that you are saying; because from your heart you are falsely inventing them."
verses.6:9: For all of them are frightening us, saying, "Their hands will grow weak from this work, and it will not be done." And now I strengthened my hands.
verses.6:10: And I entered the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Meitael, and he was shut in; and he said, "Let us gather into the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut its doors, because they are coming by night to kill you."
verses.6:11: And I said, "Who is the man who will enter into the house and live?"
verses.6:12: And I recognized, and look, God had not sent him, because the prophecy was a word against me; and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired
verses.6:13: a crowd against me, so that I might be afraid and do so and sin, and become an evil name for them, so that they might reproach me.
verses.6:14: Remember, God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of his, and Noadiah the prophet and the rest of the priests who were frightening me.
verses.6:15: And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Edud, in fifty-two days.
verses.6:16: And it happened, when our enemies heard, that all the nations around us were afraid, and fear fell greatly in their eyes, and they knew that it came about from our God that this work was finished.
verses.6:17: And in those days letters were going from many nobles of Judah to Tobiah, and those of Tobiah were coming to them;
verses.6:18: for many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and Johanan his son had taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah as a wife.
verses.6:19: And they were speaking his words to me, and they were carrying my words out to him; and Tobiah sent letters to frighten me.
verses.7:1: And it happened, when the wall was built and I set up the doors, that the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed.
verses.7:2: And I gave charge to Hananiah my brother and to Hananiah the ruler of the citadel in Jerusalem, because he was like a truthful man and feared God more than many.
verses.7:3: And I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until sunrise; and while they are still keeping watch, let the doors be shut and bolted. And station guards from those living in Jerusalem, each man at his guard post and each man opposite his house."
verses.7:4: And the city was wide and large, and the people were few in it, and houses had not been built.
verses.7:5: And God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles and the rulers and the people into companies; and I found the book of the company of those who came up at first, and I found written in it:
verses.7:6: And these are the sons of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried away, and returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each man to his city,
verses.7:7: with Zerubbabel and Jeshua and Nehemiah; Azariah, Naamiah, Nahamani, Maldocheus, Bilshan, Maspheran, Ezra, Batoei, Nahum, Baanah, Masphar. The men of the son of Israel:
verses.7:8: The sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two;
verses.7:9: The sons of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two;
verses.7:10: The sons of Arah, six hundred fifty-two;
verses.7:11: The sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua, Jobab, two thousand eight hundred eighteen;
verses.7:12: The sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four;
verses.7:13: The sons of Zathuia, eight hundred forty;
verses.7:14: The sons of Zathu, eight hundred sixty;
verses.7:15: The sons of Binnui, six hundred forty-eight;
verses.7:16: The sons of Bebai, six hundred twenty-eight;
verses.7:17: The sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred twenty-eight;
verses.7:18: The sons of Adikam, six hundred sixty-seven;
verses.7:19: The sons of Batoei, two thousand sixty-seven;
verses.7:20: The sons of Adin, six hundred fifty-five;
verses.7:21: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
verses.7:22: The sons of Hashum, three hundred twenty-eight;
verses.7:23: The sons of Bezai, three hundred twenty-four;
verses.7:24: The sons of Hariph, one hundred twelve;
verses.7:26: The sons of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three; the sons of Atopha, fifty-six.
verses.7:27: The sons of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.7:29: The men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred twenty-one;
verses.7:30: The men of Ramah and Tamal, six hundred twenty-one;
verses.7:31: The men of Michmash, one hundred twenty-two;
verses.7:32: The men of Bethel and Halia, one hundred twenty-three;
verses.7:33: The men of Nabia Aar, fifty-two;
verses.7:34: The men of Elam Aar, one thousand two hundred fifty;
verses.7:35: The sons of Harim, three hundred twenty;
verses.7:36: The sons of Jericho, three hundred forty-five;
verses.7:37: The sons of Lod, Hadia, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-one;
verses.7:38: The sons of Sananat, nine hundred thirty.
verses.7:39: The priests: the sons of Jodae, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three;
verses.7:41: The sons of Phasedur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven;
verses.7:42: The sons of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
verses.7:43: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kabdiel, of the sons of Thuduia, seventy-four;
verses.7:44: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight;
verses.7:45: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, son of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Aku, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, one hundred thirty-eight.
verses.7:46: The Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Gabaoth,
verses.7:47: the sons of Kira, the sons of Asuia, the sons of Padon,
verses.7:48: the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai,
verses.7:49: the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:50: the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,
verses.7:51: the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzzi, the sons of Paseah,
verses.7:52: the sons of Besai, the sons of Mesinom, the sons of Nephosasi,
verses.7:53: the sons of Bakbu, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harum,
verses.7:54: the sons of Basaoth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Hadasan,
verses.7:55: the sons of Barkue, the sons of Sedirath, the sons of Hemath,
verses.7:56: the sons of Aseia, the sons of Hatipha.
verses.7:57: The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
verses.7:58: the sons of Jelel, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:59: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hegel, the sons of Pochereth, the sons of Zebaim, the sons of Emim.
verses.7:60: All the Nethinim and the sons of the servants of Solomon were three hundred ninety-two.
verses.7:61: And these came up from Thelmeleth, Harsha, Cherub, Eron, Jemer, and they were not able to declare the houses of their ancestral families and their seed, whether they were from Israel:
verses.7:62: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred forty-two;
verses.7:63: and of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, because he took wives from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.7:64: These searched for their record of the company and it was not found, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
verses.7:65: And Hasersatha said that they should not eat from the most holy things until the priest should arise to give light.
verses.7:66: And the whole assembly was about forty-two thousand three hundred eight,
verses.7:67: besides their male servants and their female servants, these were three hundred thirty-seven; and male singers and female singers, two hundred forty-five;
verses.7:70: And some of the heads of the ancestral families gave to Nehemiah for the work, into the treasury, one thousand gold coins, fifty basins, and thirty mechonoth of the priests.
verses.7:71: And some of the heads of the ancestral families put into the treasury of the year twenty thousand of the gold, and two thousand two hundred minas of silver,
verses.7:72: and sixty-seven mechonoth of the priests.
verses.7:73: And the priests and the Levites and the gatekeepers and the singers and some of the people and the Nethinim and all Israel settled in their cities.
verses.8:1: And the seventh month arrived, and the sons of Israel were in their cities, and all the people gathered together as one man into the open square in front of the Water Gate. And they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which he commanded Israel.
verses.8:2: And Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women and everyone who could listen with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And he read from it from the hour when the sun shone forth until the middle of the day, facing the men and the women, and they understood; and the ears of all the people were directed toward the book of the law.
verses.8:4: And Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform, and next to him stood Mattithiah, Shemaiah, Ananiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right, and on the left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, and Zechariah.
verses.8:5: And Ezra opened the book before all the people, for he was above the people; and it happened that when he opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.8:6: And he blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people answered and said, "Amen," and they bowed low and worshiped the Lord, face to the ground.
verses.8:7: And Jeshua, Benaiah, and Sherebiah were giving the people understanding in the law, and the people were in their place.
verses.8:8: And they read from the book of the law of God, and Ezra was teaching and explaining clearly in the knowledge of the Lord, and the people understood in the reading.
verses.8:9: And Nehemiah spoke, and Ezra the priest and scribe and the Levites were giving the people understanding, and they said to all the people, "It is a holy day to the Lord our God; do not mourn or weep." For all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.
verses.8:10: And he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send a portion to those who have nothing, for the day is holy to our Lord; and do not be disheartened, for He is our strength."
verses.8:11: And the Levites were quieting the people, saying, "Be quiet, for the day is holy, and do not be cast down."
verses.8:12: And all the people went away to eat and to drink and to send portions and to celebrate with great gladness, because they understood the words that he had made known to them.
verses.8:13: And on the second day the leaders of the fathers' houses gathered together with all the people, the priests, and the Levites to Ezra the scribe, to give attention to all the words of the law.
verses.8:14: And they found written in the law which the Lord had commanded Moses, that the sons of Israel should live in booths at the feast in the seventh month,
verses.8:15: and that they should signal with trumpets in all their cities and in Jerusalem. And Ezra said, "Go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves, leaves of cypress trees, myrtle leaves, palm leaves, and leaves of dense trees, to make booths according to what is written."
verses.8:16: And the people went out and brought them, and they made booths for themselves, each man on his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the squares of the city, and as far as the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.8:17: And all the assembly, those who had returned from the captivity, made booths and sat in booths; for the sons of Israel had not done so from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, and there was great gladness.
verses.8:18: And he read from the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day until the last day; and they kept a feast for seven days, and on the eighth day a closing festival.
verses.9:1: And on the twenty-fourth day of this month the sons of Israel gathered together with fasting and in sackcloth.
verses.9:2: And the sons of Israel separated themselves from every son of a foreigner, and they stood and confessed their sins and the lawless deeds of their fathers.
verses.9:3: And they stood in their place and read from the book of the law of their God, and they were confessing to the Lord and worshiping their God.
verses.9:4: And on the steps of the Levites stood Jeshua and the sons of Kadmiel, Sherebiah son of Arabiah, and they cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
verses.9:5: And the Levites Jeshua and Kadmiel said, "Stand up, bless the Lord our God from eternity to eternity; and they will bless the name of Your glory, and they will exalt it above all blessing and praise."
verses.9:6: And Ezra said, "You Yourself are the Lord alone; You made the heaven of heaven and all their array, the earth and all that is in it, the seas and all that is in them, and You give life to all things; and the hosts of the heavens worship You.
verses.9:7: You are God; You chose Abram and brought him out of the country of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham.
verses.9:8: And You found his heart faithful before You, and You made a covenant with him to give to him the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites, and to his seed; and You confirmed Your words, for You are righteous.
verses.9:9: And You saw the humiliation of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their cry at the Red Sea.
verses.9:10: And You gave signs and wonders in Egypt, against Pharaoh and against all his servants and against all the people of his land, for You knew that they acted arrogantly against them; and You made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
verses.9:11: And You split the sea before him, and they passed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; and those who pursued them You threw into the depth like a stone in violent water.
verses.9:12: And with a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they were to go.
verses.9:13: And You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven, and You gave them right judgments and laws of truth, statutes and good commandments.
verses.9:14: And You made known to them Your holy Sabbath; You commanded them commandments, statutes, and law by the hand of Moses Your servant.
verses.9:15: And You gave them bread from heaven for their food supply, and You brought out water from a rock for them for their thirst. And You told them to enter and inherit the land over which You stretched out Your hand to give it to them.
verses.9:16: And they stiffened their neck, and they did not listen to Your commandments.
verses.9:17: And they refused to listen, and they did not remember Your wonders which You did with them; and they stiffened their neck and appointed a ruler to return to their slavery in Egypt. And You are a merciful and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in mercy, and You did not abandon them.
verses.9:18: Moreover, they even made for themselves a molten calf and said, 'These are the gods who brought us out of Egypt,' and committed great provocations.
verses.9:19: And You, in Your many compassions, did not abandon them in the wilderness; You did not turn away the pillar of cloud from them by day to lead them in the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to light for them the way in which they were to go.
verses.9:20: And You gave Your good Spirit to give them understanding, and You did not withhold Your manna from their mouth, and You gave them water for their thirst.
verses.9:21: And for forty years You sustained them in the wilderness; You did not fall short; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not split open.
verses.9:22: And You gave them kings and peoples, and You distributed to them; and they inherited the land of Sihon and that of Og king of Bashan.
verses.9:23: And You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven, and You brought them into the land which You spoke of to their fathers, and they inherited it.
verses.9:24: And You wiped out before them those who lived in the land of the Canaanites, and You gave them into their hands, both their kings and the peoples of the land, to do to them as was pleasing before them.
verses.9:25: And they captured high cities, and they inherited houses full of all good things, hewn cisterns, vineyards and olive groves, and every tree for food in abundance; and they ate and were filled and grew fat, and they delighted themselves in Your great goodness.
verses.9:26: And they shouted aloud and turned away from You, and they threw Your law behind their body, and they killed Your prophets who testified against them to turn them back to You, and they committed great provocations.
verses.9:27: And You gave them into the hand of those who afflicted them, and they afflicted them; and they cried out to You in the time of their affliction, and You heard from Your heaven, and in Your great compassions You gave them saviors, and You saved them from the hand of the one who afflicted them.
verses.9:28: And when they had rest, they returned to do evil before You; and You abandoned them into the hands of their enemies, and they ruled over them. And again they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven and rescued them in Your many compassions,
verses.9:29: and You testified against them to turn them back to Your law; and they did not listen, but sinned against Your commandments and against Your judgments, which, if a man does them, he will live by them; and they turned a disobedient back and stiffened their neck, and did not listen.
verses.9:30: And You bore with them for many years, and You testified against them by Your Spirit through the hand of Your prophets; and they did not give ear, and You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the land.
verses.9:31: And You, in Your many compassions, did not make a complete end of them and did not abandon them, for You are mighty and merciful and compassionate.
verses.9:32: And now, our God, the mighty, the great, the powerful, and the awesome, who keeps Your covenant and Your mercy, do not let all the hardship seem small before You which has found us, and our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, and our fathers, and among all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria even until this day.
verses.9:33: And You are righteous in all that comes upon us, for You have acted in truth, and we have sinned,
verses.9:34: and our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our fathers did not do Your law, and did not pay attention to Your commandments and Your testimonies which You testified to them.
verses.9:35: And they, in Your kingdom and in the abundant goodness which You gave them and in the broad and rich land which You set before them, did not serve You, and they did not turn away from their evil practices.
verses.9:36: Look, we are slaves today, and the land which You gave to our fathers to eat its fruit,
verses.9:37: belongs to the kings whom You set over us because of our sins; and they exercise authority over our bodies and over our livestock as is pleasing to them, and we are in great affliction."
verses.10:1: And in all these things we make a pledge and write it down, and our leaders, our Levites, and our priests seal it.
verses.10:2: And over those who sealed: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah
verses.10:3: son of Seraiah, and Azariah, and Jeremiah,
verses.10:9: Nadeiah, Belseiah, Shemaiah; these were the priests.
verses.10:10: And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadab, Kadmiel
verses.10:11: and his brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kanta,
verses.10:15: The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, the sons of Bani,
verses.10:16: the sons of Bani, Azgad, Bebai,
verses.10:29: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and everyone who came over from the peoples of the land to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding,
verses.10:30: prevailed over their brothers, cursed them, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all our commandments and His judgments,
verses.10:31: and not to give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons.
verses.10:32: And as for the peoples of the land who bring wares and all merchandise on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and we will forego the seventh year and the exaction of every hand.
verses.10:33: And we will establish commandments upon ourselves, to lay upon ourselves a third of a didrachma each year for the service of the house of our God,
verses.10:34: for the bread of the Presence and the continual offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the Sabbaths, of the new moons, for the feasts and for the holy things, and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for the works of the house of our God.
verses.10:35: And we cast lots concerning the lot of the wood offering, the priests and the Levites and the people, to bring it to the house of our God, for the house of our ancestral families, at times of seasons, year by year, to burn around the altar of our God, as it is written in the book;
verses.10:36: and to bring the first produce of our land and the first produce of the fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house,
verses.10:37: and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our cattle and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
verses.10:38: And the firstfruits of our grain and the fruit of every tree, of wine and of oil, we will bring to the priests, to the treasury of the house of God, and a tithe of our land to the Levites; and the Levites themselves are the ones collecting tithes in all the cities of our labor.
verses.10:39: And the priest Aaron will be with the Levite at the tithe of the Levite, and the Levites will bring up the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the treasuries, to the house of God.
verses.10:40: For the sons of Israel and the Levites will bring to the storehouses the firstfruits of the grain and of the wine and of the oil, and there are the holy vessels, and the priests and the ministers and the gatekeepers and the singers; and we will not abandon the house of our God.
verses.11:1: And the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people drew lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine parts in the cities.
verses.11:2: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
verses.11:3: And these are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem; and in the cities of Judah each man lived in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests and the Levites and the sons of the servants of Solomon.
verses.11:4: And in Jerusalem some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin lived. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Azed, son of Zechariah, son of Samariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Malelem, and of the sons of Perez.
verses.11:5: And Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Chalea, son of Hazaiah, son of Dalea, son of Joiarib, son of Thezeiah, son of Delone.
verses.11:6: All the sons of Seres who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight men of strength.
verses.11:7: And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Amesula; Joed son of Pelaiah, son of Kodiah, son of Magael, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
verses.11:8: and after him, Gabbai, Sallai: nine hundred twenty-eight.
verses.11:9: And Joel son of Zichri was overseer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
verses.11:10: Of the priests: also Dadeiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,
verses.11:11: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Apoboch, opposite the house of God.
verses.11:12: And their brothers who did the work of the house: Amzi son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah,
verses.11:13: leaders of ancestral families, two hundred forty-two. And Amasiah son of Azriel,
verses.11:14: and his brothers, mighty men of battle, one hundred twenty-eight, and the overseer was Badiel.
verses.11:15: And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Ezri;
verses.11:17: and Mattaniah son of Mica, and Obeb son of Shammua,
verses.11:19: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers, one hundred seventy-two.
verses.11:22: And the overseer of the Levites was the son of Bani, Uzzi son of Hashabiah, son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, opposite the work of the house of God.
verses.11:23: For there was a command of the king concerning them.
verses.11:24: And Pethahiah son of Baseza was at the hand of the king for every matter concerning the people.
verses.11:25: And as for the villages in their field, some of the sons of Judah also lived in Kiriath-ar,
verses.11:30: and their villages, Lachish and its fields; and they encamped in Beersheba.
verses.11:31: And the sons of Benjamin were from Gala, Michmash.
verses.11:36: And of the Levites, divisions of Judah were for Benjamin.
verses.12:1: And these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
verses.12:7: These were the leaders of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
verses.12:8: And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Machaniah; he and his brothers were over the hands for the divisions.
verses.12:10: And Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib, Joiada,
verses.12:11: and Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
verses.12:12: And in the days of Joiakim, his brothers the priests and the leaders of the ancestral houses were: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah;
verses.12:13: for Ezra, Meshullam; for Amariah, Johanan;
verses.12:14: for Amaluch, Jonathan; for Shecaniah, Joseph;
verses.12:15: for Are, Mannas; for Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.12:16: for Adadai, Zechariah; for Ganathoth, Meshullam;
verses.12:17: for Abijah, Zichri; for Mijamin, Maadai; for Piltai;
verses.12:19: for Bilgah, Shammua; for Shemaiah, Jonathan; for Joiarib, Mattenai; for Edius, Uzzi;
verses.12:20: for Sallai, Kallai; for Amok, Abed;
verses.12:21: for Hilkiah, Hashabiah; for Isdeiu, Nethanel.
verses.12:22: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Joa, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as leaders of ancestral houses, and the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.12:23: The sons of Levi, leaders of the ancestral houses, were recorded in the book of the records of the days, even until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
verses.12:24: And the leaders of the Levites: Habiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua, and the sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers opposite them, to sing hymns, to praise, by the command of David the man of God, division opposite division,
verses.12:26: in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, in the days of Nehemiah; and Ezra the priest, the scribe.
verses.12:27: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought the Levites in their places to bring them to Jerusalem, to celebrate a dedication and joy with tholatha and with songs, playing cymbals and harps.
verses.12:28: And the sons of the singers were gathered together, even from the surrounding region all around to Jerusalem, and from the villages
verses.12:29: and from the fields; for the singers built villages for themselves in Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, and the gatekeepers, and the wall.
verses.12:31: And they brought up the leaders of Judah onto the wall.
verses.12:32: And behind them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah,
verses.12:35: and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Johanan, son of Shemaiah, son of Nathaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
verses.12:36: and his brothers Shemaiah and Uzziel, to praise with the songs of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was in front of him.
verses.12:37: At the Gate of Praising, opposite them, they went up on the stairs of the cities of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David and as far as the Water Gate
verses.12:39: of Ephraim, and to the Fish Gate, and at the Tower of Hananel, and as far as the Sheep Gate.
verses.12:42: And the singers were heard, and they were inspected.
verses.12:43: And they offered great sacrifices on that day and rejoiced, because God made them rejoice greatly; and their wives and their children rejoiced, and the joy in Jerusalem was heard from far away.
verses.12:44: And on that day they appointed men over the storerooms, for the treasuries, for the firstfruits, and for the tithes, and for the leaders of the cities gathered in them, portions for the priests and for the Levites, because there was joy in Judah over the priests and over the Levites who were standing.
verses.12:45: And they kept the watches of their God and the watches of purification, and the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commands of David and Solomon his son.
verses.12:46: For in the days of David, Asaph from the beginning was first of the singers, and hymn and praise to God.
verses.12:47: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel were giving the portions of the singers and of the gatekeepers, a day's requirement in its day, and consecrating for the Levites, and the Levites were consecrating for the sons of Aaron.
verses.13:1: On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people; and it was found written in it that Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the assembly of God forever,
verses.13:2: because they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and with water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse, and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
verses.13:3: And it happened, when they heard the law, that all of mixed descent in Israel were separated.
verses.13:4: And before this, Eliashib the priest, living in a storeroom of the house of our God, was closely related to Tobiah.
verses.13:5: And he made for himself a large storeroom, and there previously they were putting the manaam, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the grain and of the wine and of the oil, the command of the Levites and of the singers and of the gatekeepers, and the firstfruits of the priests.
verses.13:6: And during all this I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king, and after the end of days I asked the king,
verses.13:7: and I came to Jerusalem; and I understood the evil, to make a storeroom for him in the court of the house of God.
verses.13:8: And it seemed very evil to me, and I threw all the goods of the house of Tobiah from the storeroom;
verses.13:9: and I spoke, and I purified the storerooms, and I returned there the vessels of the house of God, the manna, and the frankincense.
verses.13:10: And I learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and the Levites and the singers who did the work had fled, each man to his field.
verses.13:11: And I contended and said, "Why has the house of God been forsaken?" And I gathered them together, and they set them at their station.
verses.13:12: And all Judah brought the tithe of the wheat and of the wine and of the oil into the treasuries,
verses.13:13: under the hand of Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah from the Levites; and under their hand was Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Nathaniah, because they were considered faithful; it was upon them to distribute to their brothers.
verses.13:14: Remember me, God, in this, and do not let my mercy be blotted out that I have done in the house of the Lord God.
verses.13:15: In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing sheaves, and loading them onto the donkeys, as well as wine, and grapes, and figs, and every load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; and I testified on the day of their selling.
verses.13:16: And they lived in it, bringing fish and all merchandise, selling on the Sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.13:17: And I contended with the freeborn sons of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, and profaning the Sabbath day?
verses.13:18: Did your fathers not do this, and our God brought upon them and upon us all these evils, and upon this city? And are you adding wrath upon Israel by profaning the Sabbath?"
verses.13:19: And it happened, when the gates of Jerusalem were positioned before the Sabbath, that I shut the gates, and I gave word that they should not be opened after the Sabbath; and I stationed some at the gates, so as not to carry loads on the Sabbath day.
verses.13:20: And they all spent the night and made sales outside Jerusalem once and twice.
verses.13:21: And I testified against them and said to them, "Why are you spending the night opposite the wall? If you do it a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you." From that time they did not come on the Sabbath.
verses.13:22: And I spoke to the Levites, who were purifying themselves and coming, guarding the gates, consecrating the Sabbath day. For these things remember me, God, and spare me according to the abundance of Your mercy.
verses.13:23: And in those days I saw the Jews who had married Ashdodite, Ammonite, Moabite women,
verses.13:24: and half of their sons were speaking the language of Ashdod, and they did not know how to speak the language of Judah.
verses.13:25: And I contended with them and cursed them; and I struck men among them and made them swear by God, "You must not give your daughters to their sons, and you must not take any of their daughters for your sons.
verses.13:26: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin in this way? And among many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by God, and God appointed him as king over all Israel, and even him the foreign women turned aside.
verses.13:27: And we will not listen to you to do all this evil, to break faith with our God by marrying foreign women."
verses.13:28: And there were some of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest, son-in-law of Sanballat; and I expelled them from me.
verses.13:29: Remember them, God, on account of the kinship of the priesthood and of the covenant of the priesthood, and the Levites.
verses.13:30: And I purified them from everything foreign, and I established divisions for the priests and for the Levites, each man according to his work,
verses.13:31: and the gift of the wood-bearers at times from time to time and in the bacchuria. Remember me, our God, for goodness.

notes.1:1: The Greek text reads Helkiah (Chelkia) where the Hebrew has Hacaliah, Secheelu where the Hebrew has Chislev, and transliterates Hebrew habbirah ('the citadel') as abira.
notes.1:5: Greek me de (lit. 'not so, please', also in 1:11) renders an urgent Hebrew entreaty; the Greek also shifts from second person ('Your mercy') to third person ('love Him... His commandments').
notes.1:7: Greek dialysei dielysamen (lit. 'with dissolution we have dissolved') renders an emphatic Hebrew idiom for acting corruptly or destructively, and omits 'against You'.
notes.1:11: The Greek text reads eunouchos ('eunuch', attested in major Septuagint witnesses) rather than oinochoos ('cupbearer', matching the Hebrew).
notes.2:1: The Greek text reads 'before me' (Hebrew 'before him') and 'there was no one else before him' (Hebrew 'I had not been sad in his presence'), and spells Artaxerxes as Arsathertha.
notes.2:2: Greek metriazon (lit. 'being moderate') is used in Hellenistic Greek as a euphemism for being slightly unwell or indisposed; poneron and poneria (lit. 'bad/evil') here denote a sad countenance and distress of heart.
notes.2:10: This Septuagint text omits Tobiah the Ammonite servant here while retaining the plural 'to them', and in 2:12 reads 'with Israel' where the Hebrew has 'for Jerusalem'.
notes.2:13: Distinctive Septuagint readings here include 'Golela' (Hebrew 'Valley'), 'Spring of the Figs' (Hebrew 'Jackal/Dragon Spring'), and syntribon ('crushing', from reading the Hebrew verb for 'inspect' as 'shatter', also in 2:15; in 2:15 'along the wall, up the torrents' likewise reflects a distinctive Greek reading).
notes.2:20: Greek katharoi ('pure/clean') reflects a variant reading of the Hebrew consonant group translated 'we will arise' in the Masoretic Text.
notes.3:2: The Greek text lacks the verb 'built' (reading 'sons of' instead) and has 'Zabaur' for Hebrew 'Zaccur'; verse 7 of the Hebrew text is absent from this Septuagint text.
notes.3:4: Greek katecho ('hold fast', vv. 4-5) and krateo ('take hold of/strengthen', translated 'repaired' in vv. 6-32) render the Hebrew verb for repairing the wall. Verse 4 reads 'to Ramoth' (omitting Meshullam's clause), and v. 5 transliterates Hebrew 'their nobles' as Adoreem.
notes.3:15: This Septuagint text omits the first half of the verse (Shallun and the Fountain Gate) and reads 'Pool of the Fleeces for the king's shearing' where the Hebrew has 'Pool of Shelah of the king's garden'.
notes.3:26: Greek Katheinim corresponds to the Hebrew Nethinim (temple servants); here and in v. 16 the Greek reads 'garden' where the Hebrew has 'opposite', and elsewhere transliterates several Hebrew titles and terms (such as Nathurim in v. 11, Hachechar in v. 22, and Beth-eliashib in vv. 20-21).
notes.3:34: In vv. 33-37 (4:1-5 in English Bibles), the Greek text is markedly shorter than the Hebrew, spelling Sanballat as Anaballat in v. 33, placing 'Is this the army of Samaria' inside his speech in v. 34, reading 'sacrifice or eat' in v. 35, and ending abruptly in v. 37.
notes.4:4: Greek reads "the strength of the enemies" and "a large crowd" (or "much trouble"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("the strength of the burden-bearers" and "much rubble").
notes.4:7: Greek "in the sheltered places" (en tois skepeinois) contrasts with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "in the exposed/open places."
notes.4:10: Greek "the shaken-out ones" (ton ektetinagmenon) reflects the Septuagint rendering of Hebrew "young men/servants" (na'ar) via the homonymous root meaning "to shake out" (see also 5:15).
notes.4:12: Greek reads "next to him" (autou) rather than "next to me" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.4:15: Greek reads "from the rising until the dawn" with an extra "until" (heos), whereas the Hebrew text reads "from the rising of the dawn."
notes.5:5: Greek uses the feminine plural "female slaves" (doulas) for both sons and daughters, and reads "belong to the nobles" (tois entimois) where the Hebrew text reads "belong to others."
notes.5:11: Greek reads nominative "yourselves" (autoi) instead of "to them," has "from the silver" (apo tou argyriou) rather than "the hundredth part," omits "oil," and ends with the imperative "bring them out for yourselves."
notes.5:14: Greek preserves the distinct proper name "Arsenatha" (corresponding to King Artaxerxes) and renders the Hebrew term for "governor" as "extortion" (bia, also in vv. 15 and 18).
notes.5:15: Greek uses "forty didrachmas" (the standard Septuagint equivalent for shekels) and again renders servants as "shaken-out ones" (ektetinagmenoi; see 4:10).
notes.5:16: Greek has the negative "I did not take hold" (ouk ekratesa) and plural "of these people" (touton), differing from the positive Hebrew reading ("I held fast in the work of this wall").
notes.6:1: Greek reads "and no breath was left in them" (pnoe), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("no breach was left in it").
notes.6:9: Greek reads a first-person past indicative "I strengthened my hands" (ekrataiosa) rather than the imperative prayer "strengthen my hands" found in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:10: Greek "Meitael" is a distinctive Septuagint form of the name corresponding to Hebrew "Mehetabel."
notes.6:13: Continuing from 6:12, Greek reads "hired a crowd against me" (ochlon) instead of "hired him; for this reason he was hired" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.6:14: Greek spells Sanballat as "Anaballat," has singular "his deeds," makes Noadiah masculine ("the prophet"), and refers to "the rest of the priests" instead of "the rest of the prophets."
notes.6:15: Greek "Edud" is a distinctive Septuagint form of the month name corresponding to Hebrew "Elul."
notes.7:2: Greek gives both men the name Hananiah (where Hebrew has Hanani for Nehemiah's brother) and uses the loanword beira (from Hebrew birah, 'citadel, fortress').
notes.7:3: Greek heos hama to helio (lit. 'until with the sun') is an idiom for sunrise, where Hebrew reads 'until the sun is hot'; the commands to shut and bolt the doors are also passive in Greek.
notes.7:5: Greek renders Hebrew genealogical enrollment with synodia ('company, traveling party') and reads 'God' rather than Hebrew 'my God'.
notes.7:7: The Greek list has fourteen names—adding Ezra and transliterating Hebrew mispar ('number') as the name Masphar—with distinct forms Naamiah, Maldocheus, Maspheran, and Batoei, followed by 'the men of the son of Israel' (Hebrew: 'the number of the men of the people of Israel').
notes.7:33: Here and in 7:34 Greek transliterates Hebrew aher ('other') as aar (Nabia Aar; Elam Aar, with 'men' and 1,250 vs. Hebrew 'sons' and 1,254). Earlier Greek-distinct names and totals also differ from Hebrew: Jobab (7:11), Zathuia (7:13; 840), Zathu (7:14; 860), Azgad (7:17; 2,328), Adikam (7:18), Batoei (7:19), Bethlehem and Atopha split as 'sons' (7:26; 123 and 56), Kiriath-jearim's group (7:29; 721), Tamal (7:30; Hebrew Geba), and Halia (7:32; Hebrew Ai).
notes.7:40: Greek omits the family name Immer (Hebrew: 'the sons of Immer, 1,052'). Elsewhere in 7:37-45 and 7:61 Greek preserves distinct readings including Hadia (7:37), Sananat with 930 vs. Hebrew 3,930 (7:38), Jodae (7:39), Phasedur (7:41), Kabdiel and Thuduia (7:43), repeated 'Ater, son of Ater' and Aku (7:45), and Thelmeleth, Harsha, Eron, and Jemer (7:61).
notes.7:46: Nethinim transliterates Greek Natheineim (Hebrew for temple servants); in 7:46-59 Greek omits Gahar (7:49), splits Pochereth and Zebaim into two families (7:59), and preserves distinct name forms including Gabaoth, Kira, Asuia, Uzzi, Mesinom, Nephosasi, Bakbu, Harum, Basaoth, Hadasan, Barkue, Sedirath, Hemath, Aseia, Jelel, Hegel, and Emim.
notes.7:64: Greek enchisteuthesan (passive of anchisteuo, 'act as next of kin, redeem') applies the translator's standard equivalent for Hebrew g-'-l ('redeem') to its homonym meaning 'exclude as defiled.' Greek also reads 'of the company' (synodias, as in 7:5) and singular 'it was not found.'
notes.7:65: Hasersatha transliterates the Persian title ha-tirshata ('the governor') without an article, and 'to give light' (photison) renders Hebrew 'with Urim and Thummim' based on the root meaning 'light.'
notes.7:70: Greek mechonoth (also 7:72) is an untranslated transliteration (likely confusing Hebrew kothnoth, 'tunics', with mekonoth, 'stands'), with 'thirty' vs. Hebrew 'five hundred thirty' and Nehemiah as recipient rather than 'the governor' as donor. Greek also differs notably in 7:66-72: totals of 42,308 (7:66), 337 (7:67), and 2,700 donkeys (7:69, with 7:68 and camels absent); 'treasury of the year' (7:71, etous vs. ergou, 'work'); and the omission of the first part of 7:72.
notes.8:4: The Greek names Shemaiah (Samaias) and Ananiah (Anania) differ slightly from Hebrew MT Shema and Anaiah, and the Greek text lists four men on the left rather than seven.
notes.8:7: The Greek names only three Levites here (with Benaiah, Greek Banaia, corresponding to Hebrew MT Bani), whereas the Hebrew MT lists thirteen.
notes.8:8: The Greek text explicitly names Ezra as teaching and explaining clearly in the knowledge of the Lord, differing from the Hebrew MT.
notes.8:10: The Greek reads simply "for He is our strength" (or possibly "for it is our strength"), lacking the phrase "the joy of the Lord" found in the Hebrew MT and some Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:15: The Greek reads "signal with trumpets" and introduces the command with "And Ezra said," whereas the Hebrew MT has "proclaim and publish a word... saying"; the Greek also specifies "cypress trees" where MT has "wild olive."
notes.9:4: The Greek reads "the sons of Kadmiel, Sherebiah son of Arabiah" (retaining the Greek-distinct name Arabiah), whereas the Hebrew MT lists a longer series of Levite names.
notes.9:6: The Greek explicitly introduces Ezra as the speaker of the prayer ("And Ezra said"), whereas in the Hebrew MT the Levites of 9:5 continue speaking.
notes.9:21: The Greek verb is second-person singular ("You did not fall short"), referring to God's unfailing provision, whereas the Hebrew MT and some Greek witnesses read third-person plural ("they lacked nothing").
notes.9:26: The Greek reads "they shouted aloud" (elalaxan, likely a transmission shift from ellaxan, "they changed"), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "they were disobedient."
notes.9:36: The Greek text omits the clauses "and its good things; look, we are slaves in it. And its abundant produce" found in the Hebrew MT and some Greek witnesses, so "the land" in 9:36 connects directly to "belongs to the kings" in 9:37.
notes.10:3: The Greek links Zedekiah to Seraiah with "son of Seraiah," while 10:2 reads literally "over those who sealed" and omits "the governor" after Nehemiah's name.
notes.10:7: The Greek text preserves several distinct name forms in the priestly and Levitical lists: "Shebani" (10:5, MT "Shebaniah"), "Tnatoth" (10:7, MT "Ginnethon"), "Nadeiah" and "Belseiah" (10:9, MT "Maaziah, Bilgai"), "Henadab" (10:10, MT "Henadad"), and "Kanta" (10:11, MT "Kelita").
notes.10:14: Instead of MT "Hodiah, Bani, Beninu," the Greek reads "Hodum, the sons of Benjamin" and repeats "the sons of Bani" in 10:15-16; later in the lay list it reads "Aiah" (10:23, MT "Anaiah"), "Phadaeis" (10:25, MT "Pilha"), and "Ara, Hainan, Enam" (10:27, MT "Ahijah, Hanan, Anan").
notes.10:30: The Greek renders the Hebrew word for "their nobles" as a verb, "cursed them," and reads "all our commandments" without "of the Lord our Lord."
notes.10:39: The Greek reads "the priest Aaron" (omitting "son of") and ends with "to the house of God" (MT "to the house of the storehouse"); similarly, 10:35 reads "concerning the lot of the wood offering" and "in the book" (MT "in the law"), omitting "of the Lord" there and in 10:36.
notes.11:4: The Greek Judahite genealogy preserves several distinct names: "Azed," "Samariah," and "Malelem" (11:4, MT "Uzziah, Amariah, Mahalalel"), "Chalea," "Dalea," "Thezeiah," and "Delone" (11:5, MT "Col-hozeh, Adaiah, Zechariah, the Shilonite"), and "Seres" (11:6, MT "Perez," contrasting with "Perez" in 11:4).
notes.11:7: The Greek Benjaminite list reads "Amesula," "Pelaiah," "Kodiah," and "Magael" (MT "Meshullam, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah") and omits "son of" before Joed.
notes.11:11: The Greek reads "Apoboch" (MT "Ahitub") and "opposite the house of God" (taking Hebrew nagid, "ruler," as neged, "opposite"; cf. 11:22), and in 11:10 reads "also Dadeiah" (MT "Jedaiah").
notes.11:14: The Greek text of 11:12-19 is substantially shorter than the MT (omitting v. 16) and preserves distinct names: "Amasiah" and "Azriel" (11:13, MT "Amashsai, Azarel"), "Badiel" (11:14, MT "Zabdiel"), "Ezri" (11:15, MT "Azrikam"), and "Obeb" (11:17, MT "Abda").
notes.11:25: The Greek text of 11:20-36 is heavily abbreviated (omitting vv. 20-21, 28-29, and 32-35), places "the son of Bani" before "Uzzi" in 11:22, and reads "Baseza" (11:24, MT "Meshezabel"), "Kiriath-ar" (11:25, MT "Kiriath-arba"), and "Gala" (11:31, MT "Geba").
notes.12:8: Machaniah reflects the Greek name Machania (corresponding to Mattaniah in the Hebrew text; likewise Nathaniah in 12:35 and 13:13). "Over the hands" literally translates Greek epi ton cheiron, reflecting a reading of the Hebrew term for "thanksgivings" as "hands."
notes.12:15: Are and Mannas preserve distinct Greek forms of the names corresponding to Harim and Adna in the Hebrew text; verses 14-24 preserve several other Greek-distinct name forms (Amaluch, Shecaniah, Adadai, Ganathoth, Edius, Abed, Isdeiu, Joa, Habiah); verse 17 leaves Piltai unpaired, and verse 19 incorporates the names of verse 18.
notes.12:27: The term "tholatha" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "thanksgivings" (todot, with lambda for delta).
notes.12:37: "Gate of Praising" literally translates Greek pyles tou ainein (Hebrew has "Fountain Gate"), and "cities of David" preserves the Greek plural. The Greek text omits verse 38 and the beginning of verse 39, connecting "Water Gate" directly to "of Ephraim."
notes.12:44: "For the leaders of the cities gathered in them" follows the Greek tois synegmenois en autois archousin ton poleon, reflecting a reading of Hebrew "fields" as "leaders."
notes.13:5: The term "manaam" (and "manna" in verse 9) is an untranslated Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "grain offering" (minhah). In verse 4, the Greek describes Eliashib as "living in" rather than "appointed over" a storeroom.
notes.13:19: "Were positioned" renders Greek katestesan (Hebrew has "grew dark"), and "after the Sabbath" reflects the Greek omission of "until." The Greek text also leaves the direct object of "I stationed" unexpressed.
notes.13:23: "Had married" (and "by marrying" in verse 27) renders Greek ekathisan, literally "settled" or "caused to dwell," reflecting the Hebrew idiom for taking wives.
notes.13:25: "You must not give... and you must not take" renders the literal Greek oath formula "If you give... and if you take," which expresses an emphatic prohibition.
notes.13:29: "Kinship" literally renders Greek anchisteia, reflecting a reading of the Hebrew root for "defilement" as "kinship" or "redemption." In verse 31, "bacchuria" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "firstfruits" (bikkurim).
